title: Quoted Financial Product Trading Code of Conduct

tiers.name: employees
tiers.description: Directors, senior managers and employees of Turners Automotive Group Limited and its subsidiaries generally, bound by the FMCA-based insider trading prohibition described in sections 1-3, but not subject to the section 4 black-out/preclearance procedure unless also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors, the Chief Executive and all subsidiary Chief Executives/General Managers, Company management, trusts and companies controlled by such persons, and anyone else notified by the Group Financial Controller or with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling Company activities. Subject to black-out periods and mandatory written approval before any trading.

tiers.name: trusts, nominees and persons trading in another's name
tiers.description: A trust, nominee company, or another person (e.g. a family member) through or in whose name a Restricted Person intends to trade; approval must still be sought and full details of that person or entity disclosed.

windows.start_anchor: the Company's half-year balance date announcement
windows.end_anchor: first trading day after the half year results are released to NZX

windows.start_anchor: the Company's year-end balance date announcement
windows.end_anchor: first trading day after the full-year results are released to NZX

windows.start_anchor: prior to the release of a product disclosure statement for a general public offer of the same class of the Company's quoted financial products
windows.end_anchor: release of the product disclosure statement

rules.detail: 'Quoted financial products', the only products this Code's black-out and preclearance procedure covers, is defined as shares and debt instruments issued by the Company and quoted on NZX/ASX; derivatives, options or other instruments over those shares are not mentioned and are not brought within that definition.
Hedging is not named anywhere in the Code.
Monetisation transactions are not named and are not captured by the narrow 'quoted financial products' definition.
Short selling is not named anywhere in the Code.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Code.
CFDs are not named and are not 'quoted financial products' issued by the Company.
Margin lending is not addressed anywhere in the Code.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over quoted financial products is not addressed anywhere in the Code.
Secured financing arrangements are not addressed anywhere in the Code.

rules.section: 4.3 Request to Turners Automotive Group Limited
rules.detail: No fixed holding period is stated. As part of the standard preclearance application, the Company will generally decline to approve a short-term trade unless exceptional circumstances are disclosed to, and approved by, the Chair of the Audit, Risk Management and Sustainability Committee.
rules.evidence: the Company will generally not approve any trades of a short-term nature unless there are exceptional circumstances disclosed to and approved by the Chair of the Audit, Risk Management and Sustainability Committee

clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit, Risk Management and Sustainability Committee (or Chair of the Board if the applicant is that Committee's Chair); the Board may delegate approval of trades by employees below a specified seniority level to a specified senior manager
clearance.post_trade_to: Board (via a schedule of consents granted, provided by the Group Financial Controller before or at the next Board meeting); Group Financial Controller maintains a register of each request and decision
clearance.evidence: A written request on the approved form (attached) must be made and approved prior to any trading in the Company's quoted financial products. ... A trade which has been approved by the Company must occur within 5 business days after the approval has been given but may only occur whilst each of the certifications and other matters given in the application remain correct.

carve_outs: exceptional circumstances disclosed to and approved by the Chair of the Audit, Risk Management and Sustainability Committee
short_term.evidence: the Company will generally not approve any trades of a short-term nature unless there are exceptional circumstances disclosed to and approved by the Chair of the Audit, Risk Management and Sustainability Committee

exceptions.evidence: Restricted Persons are not permitted to trade any of the Company's quoted financial products during a black-out period unless the Board provides a specific exemption.

any trade of units in a managed fund or Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) will not be captured by this request/approval process. This means that investments in the Company through in your KiwiSaver, managed fund or an ETF are not captured by this section 4.3.

exemption_authority: Only the Board may grant a specific exemption for a Restricted Person to trade during a black-out period; the Code provides no authority for any officer to impose additional ad hoc black-out periods beyond the three specified (half-year results, full-year results, and pre-PDS).
jurisdiction_overlays: New Zealand Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (Part 5 insider trading, continuous disclosure, market manipulation)
ASX (secondary listing; the Code notes Australian insider trading and market manipulation laws are similar but not identical)

bespoke_clauses.clause: 'Quoted financial products' includes shares, and debt instruments issued by the Company and quoted on a financial products market operated by NZX and/or ASX. Transactions involving either of these instruments are potentially covered by the FMCA.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This Code's black-out periods and preclearance procedure are defined by reference to 'quoted financial products' and so do not, on their face, extend to an OTC put and call written by a bank; however the FMCA's own insider trading prohibition is framed more broadly around 'trad[ing] in the securities of Turners Automotive Group Limited' (section 1) and likely still catches a derivative referencing those shares as a matter of general law, separate from this Code's internal machinery.

bespoke_clauses.topic: trading through a trust, nominee or another's name
bespoke_clauses.clause: If you intend to trade in the Company's quoted financial products through a trust or nominee company, or if you intend to trade in the name of another person (for example a family member), you must still apply for approval for the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Delivering or registering the collared shares through a custodian, SPV or family trust to support the bank's security does not avoid the Restricted Person approval requirement for that underlying share movement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: directors and senior managers of the Company that acquire or dispose of a 'relevant interest' in a security of the Company must disclose that fact within five trading days of the disposal or acquisition to the NZX and in the Company's interest register.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting the bank security over the collared shares, or the collar's settlement, may itself create or change a 'relevant interest' triggering a separate five-trading-day NZX and interest-register disclosure obligation, on top of (and independent from) the Code's preclearance process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the Company makes a market announcement of price-sensitive information after the trade has been approved by the Company in accordance with this Code, then if you have not at the time of the announcement already completed that trade you must not complete that trade until at least one trading day ... after the time of the announcement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar execution approved and scheduled within the 5 business day window can still be frozen if TRA releases price-sensitive information before completion, pushing settlement into a later window.

summary: This Code's own black-out and preclearance machinery applies only to 'quoted financial products' -- shares and debt instruments issued by the Company and quoted on NZX/ASX -- and does not name or otherwise capture derivatives, hedging, monetisation, margin lending, pledges or secured financing, so nothing in the Code expressly blocks the put/call legs of a funded collar or a loan secured on the collared shares. However, any actual movement of the underlying TRA shares -- to establish collateral, on physical settlement of the written call, or otherwise -- is 'trading' in quoted financial products, and if undertaken by a Restricted Person (all directors, the CE, subsidiary CEs/GMs, and Company management) requires prior written approval from the Chair of the Audit, Risk Management and Sustainability Committee (or the Board Chair, or a delegate for junior staff), executed within 5 business days of approval, outside the three defined black-out periods (half-year results, full-year results, pre-PDS) absent a Board exemption. The Code's silence on derivatives does not extend to the FMCA's own insider trading prohibition, which is framed more broadly around trading in the Company's 'securities' and, as a matter of general law rather than this Code, may still catch an OTC derivative referenced to TRA shares while the counterparty holds material information. Short-term trades will generally not be approved absent disclosed exceptional circumstances, and routing the collateral or settlement through a trust, nominee or family member does not avoid the approval requirement. Overall, a funded collar is not expressly prohibited, but its share-settlement and collateral mechanics still need Restricted Person approval and window timing, and legal advice on the FMCA's broader reach is essential given the Code's narrow drafting.
